sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Platte County?
sections.html:
Three county offices split the job. The Assessor values property. The County Clerk builds the tax book and takes Board of Equalization appeals and tax credit applications. The Collector of Revenue mails and collects the bills.

The Collector works in the Administration Building at 415 3rd St., Room 212, Platte City, MO 64079, phone (816) 858-3356, with the counter open weekdays from 8 to 5. Assessor real estate staff answer at (816) 858-3316 until 4:30. For tax relief questions, call the County Clerk at (816) 858-3340. Questions about value, names, addresses, vehicles and tax waivers go to the assessor, and questions about missing statements go to the collector.

Platte County belongs to the Kansas City metro area, with the Missouri River along its southwestern edge and Platte City as the seat. Kansas City International Airport sits inside the county, and towns include Parkville, Weston, Riverside, Dearborn and Smithville. Four school systems serve it: Park Hill, Platte County School District Number 3, North Platte R-I and West Platte County R-II.

Home values here run high. The 2025 population estimate is 114,400, up 7.2 percent from 2020, and there are 47,969 housing units, with owners in about two thirds of them (67.4 percent). A typical owned home is valued at $345,100, median household income is $96,227 and gross rent is $1,334 a month. The county issued 425 building permits in 2025.

Statements are mailed in November, with the assessor's calendar naming November 1 as the day bills leave the Collector. They are due on receipt, and late charges start once December 31 passes. The envelope must be postmarked on or before December 31 to avoid penalty and interest. A later postmark comes back unprocessed unless penalty and interest are added.

A statement that never arrives does not remove the obligation, and trouble with the phone or web payment system does not extend the statutory deadline. Check the mailing address and legal description on each bill. If nothing has come by the end of November, call the office right away.

You can pay in person, by mail, online, by telephone using the 1-800 number printed on the bill, or at a 24-hour drop box outside the Platte County Government Complex. The counter takes cash, personal check, cashier's check, money order and credit or debit card.

The drop box is handy when the counter is closed. County closures this year fall on November 26 and 27 and December 24 and 25, so plan year-end payments around them and ask the Collector for its own holiday schedule.

Missouri law has the assessor reassess all real property on January 1 of each odd-numbered year, and Platte County's 2027 round is underway. The assessor's FAQ says the goal is equalization, not extra revenue. Early estimates put about 8,000 parcels on track for a decrease, about 900 for an increase under 1 percent, and just under 13,000 for an increase over 15 percent.

A parcel projected to rise more than 15 percent, excluding new construction, gets a written notice and an exterior inspection. An interior look happens only if the owner asks. Estimated 2027 values show on the assessor's Beacon property search beside the current 2026 value, and they may change before final values are set in early 2027.

Assessment rates are 19 percent of market value for residential, 32 percent for commercial and 12 percent for agricultural property.

The assessor describes a three-stage path, each with its own date: an informal review, then the county board, then the state.

Platte County real property appeal steps
StepWhereTiming
Informal hearingAssessor's appraisers, (816) 858-3316Before June 30
Board of EqualizationForm from the County ClerkReturned before the second Monday in July; hearings in July
State Tax CommissionComplaint for Review of AssessmentSeptember 30, or thirty days after the board rules if that is later

Bring pictures, a recent sale of your property or an appraisal to the informal meeting. An increase notice must be mailed on or before June 15. To pay under protest, the State Tax Commission guide says to pay in full by December 31, mark the check "paid under protest" and file a written statement with the collector.

sections.h2: What relief programs apply in Platte County?
sections.html:
Two county-run credits go through the County Clerk, and neither freezes value. SB-190 is the senior tax credit, which protects a qualifying participant's base-year tax liability. SB-3, the Homestead Tax Credit enacted in April 2026, targets owner-occupied primary residences not already covered by SB-190 and limits yearly tax growth to 5 percent or the Consumer Price Index, whichever is greater. Its full effect should show in the 2027 cycle.

Homes in either program are still reassessed, and a Greater Than 15% notice does not remove a participant from the credit. Call the County Clerk at (816) 858-3340 about eligibility. The state Property Tax Credit claim is separate and pays up to $1,100 to qualifying owner-occupants who are seniors or 100 percent disabled (Missouri Department of Revenue).

Get the latest bill, or look up the parcel on the assessor's Beacon search, before you list. Notices go to the owner of record at the last address the assessor has, so a seller who moved should file the assessor's change of address form so notices are not lost.

Confirm payoff figures with the Collector in Platte City, and have the title company explain how the year is split at closing. Because the statement is due on receipt, a sale in November or December leaves little time between the bill arriving and the postmark deadline. A cash purchase can close fast, but the unpaid balance still comes out of your proceeds, so settle the figure before the closing date is set.

faqs.q: When do Platte County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: Late charges begin after December 31. The envelope must be postmarked by that date, and later payments are returned unless penalty and interest are included.

faqs.q: Where do I pay in person?
faqs.a: Go to the Collector's counter in the Administration Building at 415 3rd St., Room 212, Platte City, any weekday between 8 and 5. A 24-hour drop box sits outside the entrance to the government complex.

faqs.q: Did my value go up more than 15 percent?
faqs.a: Check the Assessor's Beacon search, which shows 2027 estimates beside the 2026 value. A projected increase over 15 percent, excluding new construction, triggers a mailed notice and an exterior inspection.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for a Board of Equalization appeal?
faqs.a: The County Clerk must receive the completed form ahead of the second Monday in July. The assessor also asks owners to meet an appraiser informally before June 30.

faqs.q: Does the SB-3 Homestead Tax Credit freeze my home value?
faqs.a: No. SB-3 limits tax growth on an eligible primary residence to 5 percent or the CPI, whichever is greater, and homes in the program are still reassessed. Ask the County Clerk at (816) 858-3340 about eligibility.
